cim: Kazakhstan Hosts Aqaba Process Summit on Artificial Intelligence Security

szoveg_eredeti:
By Ayana Birbayeva in Editor’s Picks, International on 6 November 2026

ASTANA – Kazakhstan hosts an international summit on artificial intelligence security in Astana on Nov. 6, bringing together regional leaders and senior officials to discuss emerging security challenges associated with the development of AI.

Astana gathered leaders of several countries on Nov. 6 to discuss emerging security challenges. Photo credit: Akorda.

The summit was attended by Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, King Abdullah II of Jordan, Tajik President Emomali Rahmon, Turkmen President Serdar Berdimuhamedov and Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, reported the presidential press service.

Other participants included Speaker of Azerbaijan’s National Assembly Sahiba Gafarova, Kyrgyz Foreign Minister Jeenbek Kulubaev and other officials.

The Aqaba Process is an international initiative launched by King Abdullah II in 2015 to counter terrorism and violent extremism.

The platform brings together heads of state, security service chiefs, military officials and representatives of international organizations to develop a shared understanding of security threats and coordinate practical responses.
